framing: hostile second-pass on findings.json — hunt missed P0, dispute downgrades, attack scope-minimal recs

disputes.claim: Downgrade P0→P1 is wrong — food safety is binary, not graded
disputes.argument: If chef relies on items-board for batched prep (e.g. 'prepare 5 chicken nuggets'), and 1 of those has 'gluten' allergen flag, missing the flag could lead to contamination. Food safety should be P0 regardless of secondary-view status.
disputes.counter_argument: Cards view is the primary chef interface (always rendered, always allergen-visible via OrderItemResource:37). Items board is a batched-summary view, NOT used to gate prep decisions. Per project_kds_audit_2026-05-11 owner expectations: items board is informational density panel, not workflow-critical. Owner gate required to escalate P1→P0.
disputes.verdict: P1 STANDS; owner-gate escalation flag added
disputes.owner_gate_question: Is /api/admin/kds-order/items items-board view considered an allergen-safety workflow surface? Y → P0. N → P1 informational.

disputes.claim: Missing: client clock manipulation = 60s grace window bypass
disputes.argument: kds.js:71 uses now-b[itemId] >= 60000; an operator with browser devtools can set system clock backward, recall items beyond grace. Severity should be P0 because it bypasses a documented business rule.
disputes.counter_argument: Threat model: who would tamper their clock to recall? The chef themselves — and they can already do anything as authenticated workstation user. This is a self-attack, not a cross-tenant or escalation vector. Severity should reflect external threat model, not insider self-defeat. P1 stands.
disputes.verdict: P1 STANDS — clock-skew bypass noted as a sub-finding under Z1-P1-02

disputes.claim: Missing severity escalator: composition_snapshot decode runs N×items times in PHP — quadratic-ish memory at 500+ items
disputes.argument: KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::orderItems() at lines 287-326 calls safeJsonDecode(composition_snapshot) inside the groupBy callback for each item. At 50 orders × 8 items = 400 items, that's 400 JSON decodes per request. With unbounded query, could blow up to 1000+ on busy lunch.
disputes.counter_argument: JSON decode is O(n) per snapshot, snapshots are <2KB typically. 400×2KB decode = sub-millisecond total. Memory bounded by collection size. Not a P1 escalator.
disputes.verdict: P2 STANDS — perf measurement deferred to capacity planning task

disputes.claim: Severity should be P1: dispatch storm on retry creates duplicate notifications to customer
disputes.argument: Without idempotency-key, a frontend retry on flaky wifi fires Mail/SMS/Push twice. Customer receives 'Your order is ready' SMS twice. This is a user-facing defect, P1.
disputes.counter_argument: Optimistic lock on expected_status catches retry: second attempt returns 409 immediately. Mail/SMS/Push at lines 237-239 only fire if changeStatus DB::transaction succeeds (the 'changed' flag at line 233). Retry stale-status → no dispatch fired. Specifically: dispatch order is wrapped by the 'changed' flag inside transaction commit, not after retry. P2 stands.
disputes.verdict: P2 STANDS — optimistic lock prevents double-dispatch on retry of same expected_status; new dispatches only on NEW transition

disputes.claim: Hidden P0: SendOrderMail fires BEFORE OrderStatusChanged broadcast. If Mail dispatches to a queue worker that fails AFTER dispatch but BEFORE broadcast attempt, the customer gets SMS but no other system (POS, OSS, Kiosk) updates.
disputes.argument: This is the partial-success pattern: Mail/SMS/Push are dispatched (queued, not executed) before broadcast try/catch. If the DB transaction commits, all dispatches enter queue. Broadcast try/catch only protects against immediate Pusher failure. Async listener failures are separate.
disputes.counter_argument: Mail/SMS/Push and broadcast are independent queue jobs. Each retries on its own. A failed broadcast does NOT cause partial state; the OrderStatusChanged event is persisted via PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox listener (verified at app/Listeners/PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox.php) for outbox replay. Eventual consistency holds.
disputes.verdict: P3 STANDS — outbox persistence at listener level ensures eventual broadcast replay

disputes.title: NEW: KDSOrderItemsResource.resolveAddonsForKds doesn't expose composition_snapshot lines (variations) — addon-display gap on items board

evidence.code_excerpt: private function resolveAddonsForKds(): array { $snapshot = $this->safeJsonDecodeArray($this->composition_snapshot); if (isset($snapshot['addons']) && is_array($snapshot['addons'])) { return array_values($snapshot['addons']); } return []; }
evidence.missing: Equivalent resolveLinesForKds() / resolveExtrasForKds() that prefer snapshot.lines / snapshot.extras over raw item_variations / item_extras — pattern exists in OrderItemResource:65-84 but not mirrored here

disputes.impact: Items board may show variations differently from cards view if snapshot.lines exists post-T07 (legacy rows fall back). Inconsistency confusing chef.
disputes.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Mirror resolveVariationsForApi / resolveExtrasForApi pattern from OrderItemResource into KDSOrderItemsResource. Estimated 1h.

disputes.title: NEW: orderItems() does not respect branch_id filter for admin global view AT QUERY level (only at user-context filter level) — possible information disclosure under stale auth

evidence.comparison_to_sync: KdsSyncController:50-66 honors explicit ?branch_id override for admin context with cross-branch 403; orderItems() controller endpoint at KitchenDisplaySystemController.php:53-60 does NOT accept or enforce branch_id override

disputes.impact: Admin viewing items board sees ALL branches' items mixed. No branch separation. Acceptable for admin global view but a sneaky gap.
disputes.counter_argument: BranchScope global is applied on Order model per CLAUDE.md §9. Admin bypass intentional. PASS for branch isolation; the gap is UX (no branch column on items board to disambiguate), not security.
disputes.verdict: DOWNGRADED to P3 — UX clarity, not data leak
